VERDICT: Add log-only diagnostics correlating per-lead-time forecast error with cal_err failures and ranking worst settle_hours; no threshold or blend changes yet.

REASONING: Tree is settle_hour-only and hourly_wx_axes/model_break_decay are gated behind autopilot criteria, so relaxing or reweighting now is premature. The highest-value, zero-risk move is to instrument skill-by-lead-time vs calibration error to identify which hours actually drive miscalibration, giving the autopilot graduation criteria concrete evidence.

NEXT_STEPS:
1. In model_skill.py (forecast error aggregation, e.g. compute_skill_metrics/by_lead_time), add a breakdown keyed by (lead_time_bucket, settle_hour) and persist to the existing diagnostics log.
2. In calibration evaluation path (cal_err computation), join failures to the same (lead_time_bucket, settle_hour) keys and emit a correlation/attribution table — log-only.
3. Emit top-N worst settle_hours by |cal_err| weighted by trade frequency into the autopilot graduation report for hourly_wx_axes.
4. In model_blend_*.py, add a shadow log of what blend weights *would* be for the worst hours vs current settle_hour-only weights; do not apply them.
5. Gate all of the above behind a diagnostics flag; leave promotion bars and live blend logic untouched.

CALL_BACK_IF: Diagnostics show ≥3 settle_hours where cal_err breach is attributable to lead-time skill degradation with consistent shadow-blend improvement, or hourly_wx_axes/model_break_decay meet autopilot graduation criteria.
